title: Causal Map: Hazira gas terminal release and fire, 2020
audience: Investigation team, site leaders and learning leads
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document; draft: the investigation status is in progress

incident.title: Hazira gas terminal condensate release and fire

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the ProbeMatrix investigation status is in progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person. Validate before adoption.
The export mentions regulator involvement but its summary sheet says 'Reportable to Regulator: No'. Confirm the reporting status with the organisation; this pack does not decide it.
The export's Causal Chain sheet is empty. The map is built from the factor codes each finding names in its causal explanation (287 of 436 findings name other factors).

bottom_line.text: Two organisational hubs feed the most links: a culture that allowed unsafe tasks (OIC 2.1, 36 links out) and a maintenance, spares and support programme that did not hold (OIR 1.6, 26 links out). Links out are a count of links, not a measure of strength.

The pathway that matters most runs from the seal specification to the leak: no one owned the specification, supervision had no rule to enforce, the job had no guidance, and the joint went back into service on an unspecified O-ring without a test to design pressure.

Inconsistent risk management of known problems (OIC 2.7) links to supervision not responding to critical information (SVI 1.6): repeated seal failures and an open notification did not start a root-cause review.

After the release, the chain runs through command and control resources (OIR 1.1) that did not support isolation: valves that could be closed only by hand at the valve, gas detection that alarmed without acting, and an emergency plan with no isolation criteria.

sections.heading: Causal pathways
sections.intro: Each pathway reads top-down, one sentence per level, and ends on the condition at the sharp end.

items.text: No role owned the meter gasket specification or the authority to approve a substitute, and the original specification was not on file (L4) [FND-23139BF9; FND-B56701CA; EVD-8645]. Supervision had no specification, procurement or quality-control rule to enforce, so the locally bought O-ring became the regular repair part (L3) [FND-DE30BD8B; FND-852B7EC7]. At the job, the specification and a quality check for the part were not available (L2) [FND-82673283]. The 1986 flange, machined for a rectangular-slot gasket, was resealed on 18 September 2020 with an unspecified round O-ring (L1) [FND-6B3A6492; EVD-0064].

items.group: Return to service without a test
items.text: No procedure set how high-pressure meters were tested and returned to service after maintenance (L4) [FND-50C7319E; EVD-2894]. Pressurising to operating pressure had become the modelled norm, and the missing hydrostatic test was not picked up before the meter went back online (L3) [FND-71EE9734; FND-8ACDE078]. The repaired joint returned to service with a substitute seal and no hydrotest (L2) [FND-1662466D]. The joint was proved only at operating pressure and was in use when it failed (L1) [FND-4944554C; EVD-0185].

Recurring gasket failures on the meter were treated as routine maintenance, and the risk of the pattern was never assessed (L4) [FND-3A34BAD3; FND-E0AE86A6; EVD-1494]. Supervision had no trigger to turn three gasket replacements in 22 months into a root-cause investigation (L3) [FND-110F964C; FND-AC9A1E69]. The chronically failing meter stayed in service across the replacements (L2) [FND-69067A1C]. Each failure was handled as a fresh repair with the same substitute part, so the pattern produced no change (L1) [FND-8DA35CA9].

The on-site disaster management plan covered hydrocarbon leakage but gave no isolation or stoppage criteria and no delegated authority to isolate (L4) [FND-82761CC5; EVD-4052]. With no standard criteria, each responder improvised and the decision travelled up the night-shift chain (L3) [FND-D1DF4895; EVD-3932]. A steep authority gradient left people at the scene waiting for direction (L2) [FND-7505B1AF; EVD-7340]. The first emergency isolation valve was closed 46 minutes after the leak was first detected (L1) [FND-AEA16F83; EVD-6414].

The emergency isolation valves were bought and kept as local-manual valves, never upgraded for remote operation from the control room (L4) [FND-044D1DEC; FND-02310148; EVD-3932]. That design was left uncorrected (L3) [FND-DBE08E73]. Dense vapour around the leak stopped anyone approaching the source or the valves (L2) [FND-BDD73BA2; EVD-1460]. Control-room staff could not carry out the isolation from where they could safely stand (L1) [FND-F887999D].

items.group: Detection that informs rather than acts
items.text: The fire and gas detection system was provided as an annunciator display with no automatic shutdown or suppression, and was never upgraded (L4) [FND-01C3DE98; FND-4458E0C0; EVD-3452]. No policy required it to be interlocked (L3) [FND-4D7CF773]. The detection lagged the people who saw the cloud by 5 minutes and left a fully manual response (L2) [FND-B5C0CE8F; EVD-4286]. The alarm at 02:20 started a manual search, not a protective action (L1) [FND-3D785319; EVD-8657].

sections.heading: Breaks in the chain
sections.intro: Where the story needs a link the graph does not hold. Each is a gap, not a finding.

items.text: The ignition pathway is not among the top 40 links. The findings name a damaged flame-proof lamp, with three bolts missing and its glass case open, as the probable ignition source, under a breakdown-led electrical maintenance philosophy [FND-1280E788; FND-784A23E4; EVD-6916]. The export does not confirm the source.

A setting on the meter was changed and reversed during calibration in December 2019 without a record [FND-0B651843; EVD-2506]. The graph holds no link from this change to the seal failure, and the export does not say whether it bore on the joint.

The pressure transmitters on the metering lines delivered no data, so no record shows how pressure behaved in the lines before the seal failed [FND-0D4C2C13; EVD-6470]. The chain from the untested joint to the moment of failure therefore has no measured link.

sections.heading: Event sequence
sections.intro: Latent conditions, trigger, escalation and response, from dated evidence. Times on the day are from CCTV and witness statements; control-room clocks disagreed, so times are approximate.

events.text: Latent: the management-of-change procedure is published; the findings say it has not been used since 2018.
Latent: the meters are cleaned, serviced and calibrated, the first entry in the seal-repair history of the meter that later failed.
Latent: the meter is cleaned and its gasket changed; the findings say locally bought O-rings were the regular substitute.
Latent: during calibration a setting on the meter is changed and later reversed, with no mention in the signed documents.
Trigger: a notification is raised for malfunction of the meter.
Trigger: the gasket is replaced; the system is pressurised to operating pressure only, with no hydro test.
Trigger: the meter is taken back online and stays in use until the incident; the notification stays open.
Escalation: CCTV shows the vapour leak beginning at the condensate metering skid (02:12:50).
Escalation: security staff at the perimeter hear the noise and see the vapour cloud.
Response: the annunciator alarms in the Gas Terminal control room as a phone call reports the cloud; staff who go outside cannot approach the source.
Response: the shift in-charge is called by phone and the decision moves up the night-shift chain.
Response: the first emergency isolation valve is closed by hand.
Response: the pressure control valve on the 36-inch line is closed.
Escalation: the cloud ignites (03:08:15), after both isolations; the gas already released feeds the fire.
Response: active fire cooling begins, carried by the electric fire-water pumps; three of four diesel pumps are unavailable or unreliable.

gaps.text: The ignition source is named only as probable.
gaps.evidence_needed: A forensic examination record of the lamp and of the other ignition sources in the cloud's footprint.

gaps.text: No record links the December 2019 calibration change to the seal failure, or rules it out.
gaps.evidence_needed: The meter's configuration and operating-pressure history from December 2019 to September 2020.

gaps.text: No pressure data exists for the metering lines before the release.
gaps.evidence_needed: Any other pressure record for the metering lines (field gauges, upstream DCS tags) for the days before the release.

limits: Same-level links have no implied direction; read them as factors present alongside each other.
The map shows the 40 most-mentioned links of 555; a link's count is how many findings name it, not its causal weight.
A desk analysis of the published enquiry report: no site access, interviews or records beyond it.
